rfi.description: The winner of the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize, South African judge Navanethem "Navi" Pillay, tells RFI why she stands by the conclusion that Israel has committed genocide in Gaza, and why the world has a responsibility to act.

rfi.title: Louvre director says major renovation plan will be ‘extremely complex’
rfi.description: Nearly a year on from a daring jewellery heist, the Louvre museum is still trying to address serious security gaps – a significant challenge for the world’s most visited museum. Its new director says a “complex” plan is under way, but the scale of the work will require further investment.

rfi.title: Deforestation falling worldwide but Congo Basin losses grow, report finds
rfi.description: Global deforestation slowed last year, helped by gains in Latin America, but rising forest loss in Central Africa and an exceptionally strong El Nino weather pattern mean the improvement is unlikely to last, a study on Wednesday found.

rfi.title: French National Assembly moves to overhaul response to sexual violence and abuse
rfi.description: France has taken a step towards overhauling how it tackles sexual violence after MPs passed a sweeping bill without a single vote against. It would create specialist police units and courts, abuse checks in schools and leave for victims – but protections for foreign women were dropped and the cost is still unclear.

rfi.title: French counter-terrorism body to investigate 14-year-old behind school shooting
rfi.description: France's national counter-terrorism prosecutor's office announced on Tuesday that it was taking over the investigation into an attack by a student who opened fire with a shotgun on his school principal and a teacher, causing them minor injuries.

rfi.title: Ukrainian ex-officer stands trial in Germany over Nord Stream pipeline blasts
rfi.description: A former Ukrainian military officer has gone on trial, becoming the first person to face court over the 2022 explosions that ruptured the Nord Stream gas pipelines beneath the Baltic Sea.

rfi.title: France toughens fight against foreign interference as cyberattacks continue
rfi.description: France is stepping up its fight against foreign interference after cyberattacks disrupted supermarket refrigeration systems and knocked a key national security website offline. New legislation is being examined on Wednesday, a day after Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot vowed to tolerate no meddling from abroad – even from countries considered partners.

rfi.title: France and Chad sign 'renewed' defence partnership following two-year hiatus
rfi.description: French President Emmanuel Macron on Tuesday hosted Chadian leader Mahamat Idriss Déby Itno, as the two countries seek to rebuild ties two years after N'Djamena ordered French forces to leave its territory. The countries' defence ministers signed a declaration of intent to structure their defence cooperation "on a renewed basis".

rfi.title: Ex-DRC president Kabila to lead new 'politico-military' alliance with M23 rebels
rfi.description: Former Democratic Republic of Congo president Joseph Kabila has joined forces with the Rwanda-backed M23 armed group to lead a new political and military alliance, marking his most direct intervention yet in the conflict that has gripped the country’s east.

rfi.title: France intercepts Russian ‘shadow fleet’ tanker in operation off Réunion Island
rfi.description: France’s navy has boarded an oil tanker suspected of helping Russia evade Western sanctions in an operation hundreds of kilometres south of the French Indian Ocean territory of Réunion Island.

rfi.title: Champions League: Enrique urges PSG to rise to Manchester City challenge
rfi.description: Paris Saint-Germain boss Luis Enrique called on his players to rise to the challenge posed by Premier League leaders Manchester City in their second game of this season’s Champions League league phase.

rfi.description: France warned its citizens on Tuesday to avoid airports in Riyadh, Jeddah and Dammam and advised against travelling to the three Saudi cities following a series of Houthi attacks.

rfi.title: Growing concern as mosquito-borne West Nile virus gains ground in France
rfi.description: France's national health agency has recorded more than 161 cases of West Nile virus and five deaths since its annual seasonal surveillance began on 1 May. Transmitted to humans by mosquitoes, which contract it from birds, experts say global warming is fostering the spread of West Nile virus and other tropical diseases in Europe.

rfi.title: EU cautious over Trump’s ‘energy ceasefire’ as Russia continues Ukraine attacks
rfi.description: The European Union has given a cautious welcome to the prospect of an “energy ceasefire” between Russia and Ukraine, as winter approaches and renewed Russian strikes put fresh pressure on the country’s power network.

rfi.title: France braces for fresh school protests as student movement tests momentum
rfi.description: French high school students have called for another day of protests Tuesday to continue their demands for better learning conditions. Student and teacher unions have accused the government of offering no concrete solutions, while continuing to crack down on demonstrators.

rfi.title: Former Arsenal boss Wenger touted as challenger to Infantino as Fifa boss
rfi.description: Gianni Infantino could face a challenge for the presidency of Fifa, world football’s governing body, after reports on Tuesday that former Arsenal manager Arsène Wenger is preparing to stand for the post.

rfi.title: France moves to dissolve group run by anti-Semitic ideologue Alain Soral
rfi.description: France has begun proceedings to dissolve the organisation founded by French far-right anti-Semitic essayist Alain Soral, whose ideology has been cited as an influence on numerous far-right leaders.

rfi.title: Glucksmann wins French left primary to run as alternative to Melenchon
rfi.description: Centre-right politician Raphael Glucksmann has won France’s primary of the left to become the its candidate in next year's presidential elections, positioning himself as the centre-left’s main alternative to hard-left leader Jean-Luc Melenchon in the face of the rise of far right leader Marine Le Pen.

france24fr.title: Éthiopie : comment la désinformation sur les réseaux sociaux brouille la réalité de la guerre
france24fr.description: En Éthiopie, la reprise des combats au Tigré s'accompagne d'une autre bataille, moins visible mais tout aussi déterminante : celle de l’information. Sur les réseaux sociaux, des vidéos détournées, des images anciennes et des contenus générés par l'intelligence artificielle alimentent la propagande et brouillent la compréhension du conflit. Alors que l’accès au terrain reste difficile pour les journalistes, comment distinguer les faits des manipulations ? Reportage.

france24fr.title: Avec un chiffrage désormais officiel, les aides aux entreprises entrent dans le débat

Elles oscillent en 2024 entre 60 milliards et 166 milliards d'euros, selon les méthodes de calcul. Un montant considérable qui alimentera le débat de la prochaine campagne présidentielle.

france24fr.title: "Explorer massivement le Groenland": que peut Donald Trump?
france24fr.description: 3 semaines après la signature d'un accord de sécurité entre les États-Unis et le Danemark concernant le Groenland, le président Trump annonce des explorations dans le territoire autonome. Si le Groenland dispose bien de ressources en minerais et en hydrocarbures, il y a des freins juridiques, techniques et financiers à leur exploitation. De plus, des forages sur le territoire autonome danois seraient une catastrophe environnementale.

france24fr.title: Gabon : Ali Bongo conteste le gel de ses avoirs bancaires
france24fr.description: 🇬🇦 Au Gabon, Ali Bongo saisit la Commission de surveillance du marché financier de l’Afrique centrale (COSUMAF) pour contester le gel de ses comptes bancaires par BGFIBank depuis le coup d’État d’août 2023, qu’il juge illégal.

france24fr.title: Les mystérieux "Russes noirs" qui menacent la frontière entre la Biélorussie et la Lettonie
france24fr.description: Un groupe se présentant comme composé de "patriotes biélorusses", baptisé "Black Rus", a revendiqué un récent incident à la frontière entre la Biélorussie et la Lettonie. Il affirme que ce n'est qu'un début et promet d'autres actions contre des pays de l'Otan. Mais l'existence même de ce groupe soulève des interrogations, tandis qu'une possible implication des services secrets russes ou biélorusses est évoquée.

france24fr.title: Midterms 2026 : Turning Point et la bataille pour l'héritage de Charlie Kirk
france24fr.description:
Dans l'année qui a suivi la mort de Charlie Kirk, le nombre d'universités américaines comptant une antenne de Turning Point a bondi de 64 %. Mais des signes de division sont également apparus au sein de l'organisation fondée par Kirk et, plus largement, du mouvement MAGA : des figures de l'extrême droite se disputent son héritage, tandis que des théories du complot circulent autour de sa mort.

france24fr.title: Élections reportées en Haïti, pourquoi voter maintenant aurait profité aux gangs
france24fr.description: Jean-Marie Théodat, directeur du département de géographie de l'université Paris 1 Panthéon-Sorbonne et fin connaisseur d'Haïti, revient sur le report sine die des élections dans un pays placé sous la coupe des gangs. Il décrit un processus électoral devenu illusoire dans un contexte où plus de 90 % de la zone métropolitaine et une partie de l'Artibonite échappent au contrôle de l’État, évoquant une "promesse de singe" qui ne trompe personne.

france24fr.title: Ukraine : la dépendance de l'armée à Starlink en question
france24fr.description: Depuis le début de la guerre en Ukraine, Starlink s’est imposé comme un outil essentiel pour les communications de l’armée ukrainienne. Accessible et relativement peu coûteux, le réseau d’Elon Musk avait même été présenté par son patron comme un moyen de soutenir les soldats ukrainiens. Mais cette dépendance à une technologie privée pose aujourd’hui question : que se passe-t-il lorsqu’un acteur privé peut influer sur les capacités militaires d’un pays ? Et plus largement, quel risque représente

france24fr.title: Inde : deux dirigeants du Parti des Cafards arrêtés après un week-end de manifestations
france24fr.description: En Inde, le Parti des Cafards, devenu un symbole de la contestation menée par la jeunesse, dénonce la répression du gouvernement de Narendra Modi. Après l’arrestation de milliers de manifestants ce week-end, deux dirigeants du mouvement ont été placés en détention à New Delhi. Depuis plusieurs semaines, l’opposition se mobilise contre une révision des listes électorales, accusée de favoriser le parti au pouvoir.

france24fr.title: Hospitalisé, le Pape Léon XIV pourra-t-il réaliser sa visite en Amérique Latine ?
france24fr.description: Le pape Léon XIV, opéré d’un nodule cancéreux au poumon, est toujours hospitalisé et l’incertitude demeure sur la suite de son programme. Sa visite prévue en Amérique latine, qui doit l’emmener dans plusieurs pays, soulève notamment des questions : certaines étapes, comme Cusco au Pérou, située à 3 400 mètres d’altitude, pourraient être délicates compte tenu de son état pulmonaire.

france24fr.title: France-Tchad : vers une relance de la coopération militaire
france24fr.description: La France et le Tchad relancent leur coopération militaire, deux ans après la rupture de leur accord de défense et le retrait des troupes françaises du pays. Les deux États ont signé à Paris une déclaration d’intention pour définir de nouveaux axes de coopération, dans un contexte où N’Djamena cherche à diversifier ses partenaires militaires. Pour Paris, l’enjeu est de renouer des liens avec un allié stratégique au Sahel.

france24fr.title: Le Costa Rica inaugure une méga-prison sur le modèle de celles du Salvador
france24fr.description: Le Costa Rica inaugure une méga-prison inspirée du modèle salvadorien, conçue pour accueillir environ 5 000 détenus. Sans prises électriques dans les cellules et avec un contrôle strict de la nourriture et des vêtements autorisés, l’établissement vise à empêcher les détenus de communiquer avec l’extérieur et à couper les liens entre les chefs de gangs et leurs réseaux criminels. Le Costa Rica devient un pays de plus en plus répressif, avec un taux de criminalité en hausse, comme l'explique la co

france24fr.title: Violences sexuelles : les nouvelles mesures pour accompagner les victimes en France
france24fr.description: Le 13 octobre, l’Assemblée nationale a adopté à l’unanimité la loi intégrale contre les violences sexistes et sexuelles (VSS). Quels changements concrets prévoit ce texte pour les victimes ? Entretien avec Céline Thiébault-Martinez, rapporteure générale de la proposition de loi, sur les dispositifs mis en place pour mieux accompagner les victimes et construire une chaîne judiciaire spécialisée, de la prise en charge au suivi. L’objectif : leur rappeler qu’elles ne sont pas seules et que la socié

france24fr.title: Procès en Irak de djihadistes français : nouvelle audience pour les accusés
france24fr.description: En Irak, le procès de six djihadistes français se poursuit à Bagdad. Un seul des six hommes, tous emmenés en Syrie alors qu’ils étaient mineurs, a été présenté devant le juge ce mercredi. Arrêtés en 2018 par les Forces démocratiques syriennes, ils ont ensuite été transférés en Irak. Une affaire sensible, qui soulève des enjeux judiciaires entre Paris et Bagdad autour du sort de ces détenus français. Les précisions de Marie-Charlotte Roupie depuis Bagdad.

france24fr.title: Tchad - France : reprise de la collaboration militaire
france24fr.description: Le Tchad et la France reparlent coopération militaire. Près de 2 ans après l'éviction de l'armée française, les deux pays ont signé hier une déclaration d’intention. Un projet porté par Emmanuel Macron et Mahamat Idriss Déby qui multiplient les rencontres.

france24fr.title: Budget en France : le casse-tête à l'Assemblée
france24fr.description: Entre mobilisation lycéenne, inquiétudes sur le pouvoir d’achat et craintes d’une crise financière, le gouvernement présentait ce mardi son projet de budget pour 2027. Son adoption s’annonce particulièrement incertaine, faute de majorité parlementaire et à l’approche de la présidentielle. Déjà confronté à l’impasse budgétaire l’an dernier, Sébastien Lecornu peine à convaincre les oppositions, qui imputent la situation à dix ans de macronisme. Analyse de Roselyne Febvre.

france24fr.title: Ukraine : pétrole russe contre renseignement, le chantage américain ?
france24fr.description: L’Ukraine a de nouveau été frappée par des attaques russes meurtrières sur Kiev, qui ont fait au moins 12 morts et privé des centaines de milliers de foyers d’électricité. Dans le même temps, des responsables ukrainiens laissent entendre que Washington ferait pression sur Kiev pour qu’elle cesse de viser les raffineries russes, sous peine de voir les États-Unis suspendre leur partage de renseignements. Analyse de Bruno Daroux.

france24fr.title: Israël : la Colombie du président Abelardo de la Espriella inaugure son ambassade à Jérusalem
france24fr.description: La Colombie a inauguré mercredi son ambassade à Jérusalem, rejoignant le cercle restreint des pays disposant d'une représentation diplomatique auprès des autorités israéliennes dans cette ville dont le statut de capitale d'Israël n'est pas reconnu par la communauté internationale. Le nouveau président Abelardo de la Espriella a rétabli les liens diplomatiques avec Israël cet été. Ils avaient été rompus en 2024 par son prédécesseur pour dénoncer l'offensive militaire dans la bande de Gaza.

zeit.description: Gesundheitsminister Linnemann hat sich zur Entwicklung des Zusatzbeitrags geäußert. Der GKV-Schätzerkreis hatte einen unveränderten Beitrag von 2,9 Prozent empfohlen.

zeit.description: Seit den verlorenen Landtagswahlen müht sich Friedrich Merz, die Reformen neu zu verkaufen. Im Bundestag zeigt sich, woran es dem Kanzler dabei fehlt: Glaubwürdigkeit.

zeit.description: Bestsellerautorin Sally Rooney stellt sich gegen die Einstufung einer propalästinensischen Gruppe in Großbritannien. Ihre Bücher werden dort nicht mehr verkauft.

zeit.description: Soll sich Hamburg ein neues Naturkundemuseum leisten, in diesen knappen Zeiten? Ja, sagt Bernhard Misof, Direktor des Instituts hinter dem Museum. Hier erklärt er, wieso.

spiegel.title: Krankenversicherung: Zusatzbeitrag kann 2027 stabil bleiben
spiegel.description: Der durchschnittliche Zusatzbeitrag für die gesetzliche Krankenversicherung muss nicht erhöht werden. Gesundheitsminister Carsten Linnemann sieht das als gutes Zeichen. Die Finanzlage der Kassen sei dennoch angespannt.

spiegel.title: Netflix streicht rund 1000 Jobs
spiegel.description: Beim Streamingkonzern Netflix sollen weltweit sechs Prozent der Stellen wegfallen. Die Chefs begründen das mit Disziplin und Prioritätensetzung.

spiegel.title: Pkw-Maut-Prozess gegen Andreas Scheuer: Zeuge weist Vorwurf der Rachsucht zurück
spiegel.description: Wollte der Eventim-Chef CSU-Politiker Andreas Scheuer schaden? Im Prozess um die gescheiterte Pkw-Maut weist der als Zeuge geladene Unternehmer den Vorwurf der Rachsucht zurück.

spiegel.title: Aufregung um Ledger: Warum Krypto-Käufer panisch Hardware-Wallets auseinandernehmen
spiegel.description: Lange galt eine Verwahrmethode für Kryptowerte als recht sicher: Hardware-Wallets. Jetzt erregt eine aufwendige Attacke Aufsehen, über 100 Millionen Dollar fehlen. Die Schockwellen reichen bis zu Saturn und MediaMarkt.

spiegel.title: Ukraine: Wie sich die Menschen in Kyjiw auf den Kriegswinter vorbereiten
spiegel.description: US-Geheimdienstinformationen flossen zuletzt nicht wie gewohnt, darum sieht sich die Ukraine Russlands Luftangriffen zunehmend hilflos ausgeliefert. Die Einwohner von Kyjiw treffen Vorkehrungen, manche verlassen die Stadt.

spiegel.title: Abi in Hamburg: Schulen sollen bald Ukrainisch als Abiturfach anbieten
spiegel.description: Mehr als 5000 ukrainischsprachige Kinder und Jugendliche besuchen derzeit Schulen in Hamburg. Die Bürgerschaft will die Sprache nun als Prüfungsfach im Abitur anerkennen lassen.

spiegel.title: Radsport: Valentina Cavallar beklagt Dopingprobe kurz nach dem Tod ihrer Mutter
spiegel.description: Radrennfahrerin Valentina Cavallar hat eine für sie verstörende Dopingkontrolle öffentlich gemacht und den Umgang mit Profisportlern kritisiert. Die zuständige Agentur bat nach Medieninformationen um Entschuldigung.

spiegel.title: Dagi Bee: Influencerin fahndet via Instagram nach zwei Männern – Polizei kritisiert solche Aktionen
spiegel.description: Die Polizei rät von solchen Aktionen ab: Die Influencerin Dagi Bee wurde laut eigener Aussage Opfer einer Straftat und teilt ein Video der mutmaßlichen Täter mit der Bitte um Hinweise. Einer der Männer trägt einen Labubu-Hoodie.

spiegel.title: Sondierungen mit Linke gehen weiter: Grüne Bundesspitzen sind sauer auf Berliner Grüne
spiegel.description: Die Grünen in Berlin möchten die Sondierungen mit der Linken fortführen. Co-Bundeschef Banaszak und weitere Führungspolitikerinnen zeigen sich über die Entscheidung verärgert.

spiegel.title: Friedrich Merz: Der Kanzler sucht eine neue Erzählung für seine schwarz-rote Koalition
spiegel.description: Friedrich Merz ist auf der Suche nach einer neuen Story für seine angeschlagene Koalition. Die Sache hat nur einen Haken.

spiegel.title: Hamburg: Er kritisierte seine Partei vehement. Jetzt könnte er seinen Posten verlieren
spiegel.description: Jahrelang zahlte die Parteispitze der Hamburger Grünen nicht in die Sozialkassen ein. Ein Mitglied rebellierte dagegen und drohte mit Klage. Manchen in der Partei gilt er nun als Nestbeschmutzer.

spiegel.title: Landtag von Sachsen-Anhalt: Der AfD-Parlamentspräsident daddelt auf seinem Handy
spiegel.description: In Sachsen-Anhalt haben AfD und BSW ihr erstes gemeinsames Projekt durch den Landtag gebracht. Der Beschluss ist politisch weitgehend folgenlos, eine äußerst aufschlussreiche Sitzung war es dennoch.

spiegel.title: Wohnen mit Kindern: Wie drei Teenager unser Zuhause in eine Dauer-WG verwandelt haben
spiegel.description: Wir hatten liebevoll eingerichtete vier Wände mit teuren Möbeln und ausgewählten Lieblingsstücken. Bis drei Teenager die Herrschaft über sämtliche Flächen übernommen haben. Also mieteten wir eine zweite Wohnung.

spiegel.title: Sally Rooney stoppt Verkauf ihrer Bücher in Großbritannien
spiegel.description: Die Bestsellerautorin Sally Rooney hat sich mit der britischen Protestgruppe »Palestine Action« solidarisiert. Nun befürchtet sie, dass der Verkauf ihrer Werke im Königreich als Terrorfinanzierung gewertet werden könnte.

spiegel.title: Israel: Ex-Geheimdienstchef klagt gegen Netanyahu im Streit über Warnungen am 7. Oktober
spiegel.description: Hat Israels Ministerpräsident Warnungen vor einer Invasion der Hamas im Oktober 2023 nicht ernst genommen? Der frühere Schin-Bet-Chef Ronen Bar erhebt nun neue Vorwürfe und wirft Netanyahu Verleumdung vor.

spiegel.title: News des Tages: Zuckersteuer, Ärger um Linke Abgeordnete Emde, Ende des McRib, Bayern-Superstar Michael Olise
spiegel.description: Schwarz-Rot beschließt die Zuckersteuer, Cola und Limo werden teurer. Die Linke in Berlin versinkt im Tohuwabohu. Und Fußballdeutschland wundert sich: Olise zeigt Nerven? Das ist die Lage am Mittwochabend.

spiegel.title: Sachsen-Anhalt: So lief die erste Sitzung im AfD-geführten Landtag in Magdeburg
spiegel.description: AfD und BSW haben im neuen Landtag von Sachsen-Anhalt erstmals gemeinsame Sache gemacht. SPIEGEL-Korrespondent Peter Maxwill berichtet von der aufgeheizten Stimmung vor Ort.

spiegel.title: Deutsche Bahn: An Bahnhöfen gilt jetzt bundesweit ein Alkoholverbot – was bedeutet das?
spiegel.description: An allen 5700 Bahnhöfen der Bahn darf von Donnerstag an kein Alkohol mehr getrunken werden. Aber wie will die Bahn das durchsetzen? Und welche Strafen drohen bei Verstößen? Die wichtigsten Antworten.

nzz.title: Harmlose humoristische Dorfposse oder Herabsetzung der jüdischen Gemeinschaft? Zürcher Gericht urteilt über den Inhalt einer Kurzgeschichte
nzz.description: Ein 89-jähriger Autor und ein 77-jähriger Redaktor einer Zeitschrift waren aufgrund einer veröffentlichten Kurzgeschichte wegen Diskriminierung angeklagt. Der Richter spricht sie frei – obwohl er den Text als problematisch einstuft.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Iran-Krieg: Frachtschiff sinkt in Strasse von Hormuz wegen Seemine
nzz.description: Die USA und Iran befinden sich seit Februar 2026 im Kriegszustand. Zwar haben die beiden Länder eine Waffenruhe vereinbart, doch Donald Trump hat diese Anfang Juli für beendet erklärt. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Ticker.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Crans-Montana: Jessica Moretti fordert Taggeld von ihrer Unfallversicherung
nzz.description: In der Bar «Le Constellation» in Crans-Montana im Wallis ist es in der Neujahrsnacht zu einem verheerenden Brand gekommen. 41 Personen sind ums Leben gekommen. Die Ermittlungen laufen. Das sind die neuesten Entwicklungen.

nzz.title: BILDSTRECKE - Die Schülerproteste in Frankreich dauern an
nzz.description: Was Ende September 2026 als friedliche Proteste begann, hat sich inzwischen zu einer landesweiten Massenbewegung entwickelt. Zehntausende fordern bessere Bedingungen an Frankreichs Schulen.

nzz.title: DER ANDERE BLICK - Die Berliner Linkspartei zeigt, dass man mit ihr nicht zu verhandeln braucht
nzz.description: In der deutschen Hauptstadt müssen SPD und Grüne erkennen, dass Die Linke es bei der Bekämpfung des Antisemitismus nicht ernst meint.

nzz.title: Albert Rösti reagiert auf Kritik und will Kinder und Jugendliche in sozialen Netzwerken nun doch besser schützen
nzz.description: Damit geht der Bundesrat auf Kritik aus der Vernehmlassung ein. In einem ersten Entwurf fehlte der Jugendschutz komplett. Die Schweiz sieht für die Plattformregulierung eine liberalere Lösung vor als die EU.

nzz.title: Spaniens König besucht Ceuta – und wird ungewöhnlich deutlich
nzz.description: Zum ersten Mal in seinem Leben setzt König Felipe VI. Fuss auf den Boden der spanischen Exklaven. Dort waren er und seine Frau Letizia nach der Migrationskrise vom Sommer sehnlichst erwartet worden. Für das Königshaus in Wahlkampfzeiten eine heikle Mission.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Liebesaffäre in Lausanne: Das Bundesgericht ist endlich aufgewacht
nzz.description: Das höchste Gericht steckt seit Monaten tief in der Krise. Nun versucht es mit einer neuen Führung den Neuanfang. Das lässt hoffen.

nzz.title: ERKLÄRT - Der Papst hat ein Lungenkarzinom. Welche Prognose hat er? Wie kann man diesen Tumor entdecken, und wer sollte zur Vorsorgeuntersuchung?
nzz.description: Lungenkrebs ist eine der häufigsten Todesursachen weltweit. Nun wurde auch der Papst wegen der Krankheit operiert. Was ist über den Fall bekannt? Wir haben die wichtigsten Fakten zusammengetragen.

nzz.title: MELDUNGEN WIRTSCHAFT - Netflix kündigt grössten Stellenabbau in seiner Geschichte an +++ Lufthansa erwirbt Anteil an portugiesischer Fluggesellschaft
«Müllermilch»-Erbe blitzt mit Anzeige gegen Komiker Mike Müller ab
nzz.description: Der im Kanton Zürich lebende Sohn des deutschen Unternehmers zeigte den Komiker wegen Verleumdung an. Grund war ein Post in den sozialen Netzwerken.

nzz.title: BILDSTRECKE - Erneut tödlicher Angriff auf Kiew ohne Vorwarnung – Bilder des Krieges in der Ukraine
nzz.description: Die russische Invasion führt bereits im fünften Jahr zu Hunderttausenden Toten und der Zerstörung ganzer Städte. Die neuesten Entwicklungen in Bildern.

nzz.title: MELDUNGEN POLIZEI - Brand in Schulhaus in der Stadt Zürich – Gebäude ist zurzeit nicht nutzbar
nzz.description: Die neuesten Polizeimeldungen aus der Schweiz.

nzz.title: Die Ukraine gerät unter massiven Druck der USA: Einschränkungen beim Starlink-Internet behindern den Kampf gegen Russland
nzz.description: Präsident Donald Trump kritisiert die ukrainischen Angriffe auf russische Raffinerien. Nun will er Kiew offenbar zu einem Stopp zwingen – und dies, obwohl Russland täglich den von Trump verkündeten «Energie-Waffenstillstand» bricht.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Lage im Gazastreifen: Israel greift Ziele in Gaza Stadt an – unter den Getöteten soll auch ein Hamas-Mitglied sein
nzz.description: Die Waffenruhe zwischen Israel und der Hamas ist instabil, die humanitäre Not im Gazastreifen ist gross. Der Friedensplan der USA wurde bisher nur teilweise umgesetzt. Die wichtigsten Fragen und Antworten.

observador.title: Ministério da Educação incendiado em confrontos em Tirana
observador.description: É o segundo dia de protestos de estudantes universitários na capital da Albânia. Os confrontos entre manifestantes e polícia já levaram a pelo menos 20 detenções. O Ministério da Educação incendiado.

observador.title: Betis-FC Porto. Farioli faz quatro alterações na equipa
observador.description: 100% vitorioso na Liga mas com uma derrota na Champions diante do City, FC Porto procura o primeiro triunfo na prova frente ao Betis no La Cartuja, onde ganhou Taça UEFA de 2003. Siga aqui em direto.

observador.title: "Ficamos muito satisfeitos, mas aguardamos mais detalhes"
observador.description: Manuel Mourato, autarca de V. N. da Barquinha, saúda a abertura da pista de Tancos à aviação civil. Destaca o dinamismo para a região, mas aguarda os esclarecimentos do Governo, em reunião a agendar.

observador.title: OE. PS diz que retirou ao Chega possibilidade de chantagear
observador.description: O deputado socialista Carlos Pereira afirma que o OE "dá, neste momento, ao PS tranquilidade para haver paz política" e diz que Chega está "aflito" por não ter muito poder na matéria.

observador.title: O que ganha Portugal com a privatização da TAP?
observador.description: Filipe Costa (PS) rejeita privatização total e defende os 49,9%. Jorge Miguel Teixeira (IL) defende venda a 100%, mas pede clareza. Gonçalo Lage (PSD) rejeita dúvidas e destaca o potencial da TAP.

observador.title: EUA levantam sanções ao presidente do parlamento venezuelano
observador.description: Departamento do Tesouro retirou o dirigente venezuelano da lista de sancionados. O irmão de Delcy Rodríguez estava na lista desde setembro de 2018.

observador.title: UE cria alerta que permite partilhar dados sobre terrorismo
observador.description: A partir desta quinta-feira, o SIS passa a integrar informações de parceiros externos sobre suspeitos de terrorismo e criminalidade organizada grave, com apoio da Europol.

observador.title: Certificação florestal pode favorecer a biodiversidade
observador.description: Investigadores do CESAM analisaram florestas em todo o mundo e em Portugal. Mais diversidade vegetal e presença de água são fatores-chave para a vida selvagem.

observador.title: 18h. TAP. Lufthansa disposta a comprar totalidade da empresa
observador.description: Companhia vencedora da privatização da TAP saúda decisão do Governo e antevê um futuro de sucesso. Ainda, Mário Centeno critica mudanças recentes na Educação, que criaram “problemas que não existiam”.

observador.title: Defesa quer inovação militar e Portugal nas redes da NATO
observador.description: Portugal atingiu em 2025 a meta de investimento de 2% do PIB na defesa. Mas Nuno Melo ressalva que "o investimento só por si significa pouco". "Quem não evolui, perde no campo de batalha", advertiu.

observador.title: NATO. Investigação de fraude leva a 5 detenções e buscas
observador.description: A Eurojust estima prejuízos de cerca de um milhão de euros para Estados-membros. Uma empresa suspeita terá subornado funcionários para obter tratamento privilegiado da NSPA.

observador.title: Contabilista: corte de 50% no IRS leva a menores acertos

phys-org.title: Same-day heat wave and wildfire smoke exposure is increasing worldwide
phys-org.description: Europe's heat waves this past summer broke countless records, and wildfires spread across Spain and France, forcing mass evacuations.

phys-org.title: Storm Harry: Drifting buoys help improve early forecasts of extreme events in the Mediterranean Sea
phys-org.description: A network of drifting buoys equipped with barometers can help improve weather forecasts of extreme Mediterranean storms by providing crucial atmospheric observations from areas of the sea where measurements are scarce. A new study published in the Quarterly Journal of the Royal Meteorological Society provides the first assessment of the impact of these observations during Storm Harry, which affected the Mediterranean region in January 2026.

phys-org.title: Scientists establish new genus of deep-sea 'spaghetti worms'
phys-org.description: Scientists have announced a new genus of deep-sea segmented marine "spaghetti worms" with suction cups on their bodies, showing just how much undiscovered biodiversity is out there in the deep seas around Australia.

phys-org.title: Software advance brings complex quantum simulations to standard computers
phys-org.description: A major software advance could aid the creation of bigger, more reliable quantum computers, a study suggests. Researchers have developed an algorithm that enables off-the-shelf computers to run quantum simulations previously only possible using the world's most powerful supercomputers.

phys-org.title: Fighting off microbial invasions drains plants' iron stores, but one protein helps restore balance
phys-org.description: Energy production in our cells, oxygen traveling in our blood and immune cells fighting infection all depend on iron, an essential mineral that enters the food chain when plants absorb it from soil. But iron is often scarce—likely increasingly so as global weather and temperatures continue to change—and we aren't the only ones that need it.

phys-org.title: Bering Land Bridge base camp reveals what life was like nearly 14,000 years ago
phys-org.description: The area of water between Russia and North America and the Pacific and Arctic oceans is now known as the Bering Strait. Yet it was once what we call the Bering Land Bridge, an exposed land and maritime region that connected Asia to North America.

phys-org.title: Main factors in pornography use among adolescents identified
phys-org.description: A study by the Universitat Rovira i Virgili (URV) has analyzed which factors are most associated with pornography use during adolescence. The results show that the most predictive variable is gender, followed by problematic internet use, cannabis and alcohol consumption, family conflict and engaging in certain risky sexual behaviors. The research, published in the journal Computation, was based on the 2023 ESTUDES survey and used a sample of 33,543 adolescents. The aim was to determine which per

phys-org.title: New DNA tool could help detect harmful algal blooms before they spread
phys-org.description: A new study by researchers at the University of South Florida and Florida Atlantic University has demonstrated that a DNA sequencing tool can rapidly identify harmful algae in coastal waters, offering a new approach for monitoring species that could lead to improved methods for detecting potentially dangerous species before blooms become widespread.

phys-org.title: Removing rats and restoring native plants could help atolls withstand rising seas
phys-org.description: Protecting seabirds and restoring natural vegetation could give low-lying tropical atoll islands a fighting chance against the threat of sea-level rise, a new study reveals.

phys-org.title: Warmer coastal waters drive heavy cyclone rainfall farther inland, raising flood risks
phys-org.description: A research team at The Hong Kong Polytechnic University (PolyU) has found that the area affected by tropical cyclone (TC) rainfall is extending inland along Northern Hemisphere coasts at an average rate of approximately 3.8 kilometers (2.4 miles) per decade. Driven by rising nearshore sea surface temperature (SST), this shift is increasing disaster risks for inland regions. The work is published in the journal Nature Communications.

phys-org.title: Nine studies reveal consumers favor eco-friendly additions over waste-cutting removals
phys-org.description: When hotels replace single-use toiletries with refillable dispensers, or companies strip unnecessary items from product bundles to cut waste, they may expect consumers to hail these changes as environmentally responsible.

phys-org.title: Bacteria turn 3D-printed sand into solid building elements
phys-org.description: Cement manufacturing is one of the largest sources of CO₂ emissions in the construction industry. At the Department of Architecture, Karen Antorveza Paez, who has just completed her doctorate at ETH Zurich, is researching an alternative that works in a different way: instead of firing rocks at over 1,000°C, she is getting bacteria to bond grains of sand together into solid architectural elements.

phys-org.title: Gathering rare airborne observations of firestorm clouds
phys-org.description: Just minutes into a planned research flight from Colorado to Oregon in August to study massive storm clouds fueled by intense wildfires, scientists discovered that a fire in Utah offered a more promising target. phys-org.title: 'Sundown towns' linked to lingering racial bias
phys-org.description: A sundown town is a community that prohibited Black people from staying within its borders after dark or from owning property. This was done through laws, signs, threats, harassment or violence. More than 150 years after the end of slavery and a generation after Civil Rights reforms, a new study finds that places designated as "sundown towns" in the past are more racist today.

phys-org.title: Toothless 'hell chicken' dinosaur may have had a taste for fruit
phys-org.description: While many dinosaurs were fearsome predators with razor-sharp teeth, others were peaceful herbivores munching on plants. We can now add a new species to the list of plant-eaters, Infernogallus jamesi. Its name means hell chicken, and its fossilized remains were found in the Hell Creek Formation, a fossil-rich rock formation extending across parts of Montana, South Dakota and North Dakota. And it is providing fresh insights into how some dinosaur diets evolved.

phys-org.title: Local DNA motion inside the cell stays nearly constant throughout interphase
phys-org.description: Human genomic DNA is wrapped around core histone proteins to form nucleosomes, the fundamental units of chromatin. During interphase, the period between cell divisions, DNA is replicated and the nucleus becomes larger. At the same time, cells must continuously carry out essential genome functions such as transcription, DNA replication and DNA repair. How the behavior of genomic DNA is maintained during these large changes has remained unclear.

phys-org.title: How drought shapes the impact of Xylella fastidiosa on almond trees
phys-org.description: Xylella fastidiosa is a pathogen that poses a serious threat to agri-food systems. An insect-borne bacterium that eventually causes trees to dry out and die, it was first detected in Spain in 2016, alarming the farming community. Although it is more commonly associated with olive trees, it also inflicts heavy losses on almond crops.

phys-org.title: Australia's oldest underwater archaeology reveals ancient life within a lost landscape
phys-org.description: New discoveries from Australia's oldest known underwater archaeological record reveal how First Peoples lived, transported goods and used different places within a vast cultural landscape that was submerged when rising seas transformed the continent after the last ice age.

undark.title: Podcast: Which Animals Are Conscious?
undark.description: This week on the show, our hosts talk to Heather Browning, a philosopher at the University of Southampton in the U.K, and Deb Brown, a philosopher and the  director of the Critical Thinking Project at the University of Queensland in Australia, about which animals feel pain and more.

undark.title: Podcast: Is ADHD Actually a Disorder?
undark.description: On Entanglements this week: Barbara Franke, a professor of molecular psychiatry at Radboud University in the Netherlands, and Edmund Sonuga-Barke, a developmental psychologist and a professor at King’s College London discuss whether ADHD should be considered a disorder.

undark.title: Podcast: Should We Put AI-Enabled Tech in Our Brains?
undark.description: Welcome to Season 3 of Entanglements! In our first episode, we discuss neural implants and AI with Judy Illes, a professor of neurology and neuroethics at the University of British Columbia, and Joseph J. Fins, a physician scientist and medical ethicist at Weill Cornell Medicine in New York.

undark.title: Engineering Animals to Grow Human Organs — But Not Human Minds
undark.description: Chimeras, or animals with human cells and tissues, are not new, and researchers have long used them to gain insights into diseases and even as a potential source of transplantable organs. But the research brings up thorny ethical questions regarding animal rights and the moral status of chimeric creatures.

undark.title: AI-Driven Biology Is Only as Good as the Data Beneath It
undark.description: Opinion | The biotech and pharma industries are pouring billions of dollars into AI-driven drug discovery and development. But the genomic data used to train AI models are often incomplete, contain errors, or lack contextual information — a quality issue that threatens to slow the pace of biological research.

undark.title: In Italy, What Earth Can Tell Us About Extraterrestrial Life
undark.description: Photo Essay | From sampling hydrothermal vents and abandoned mines to lab experiments that replicate Mars’ atmosphere, scientists are using what we know about life on Earth to understand how it may exist on other worlds. Italy, it seems, provides particularly fertile ground for such explorations.

undark.title: The Evolving Quest to Build Life in a Lab
undark.description: Scientists are trying to create new life, whether to understand how biology first developed on Earth, or design new cells from scratch.  But life hasn’t happened — at least not yet. And questions around safety, as well as what even constitutes life in the first place, continue to swirl.

undark.title: The Embryos That Don’t Come From Eggs and Sperm
undark.description: Human embryo models mimic the earliest development stages; they could offer a glimpse of the first weeks of pregnancy — a mysterious period for which natural embryos are seldom available — and potentially shed light on miscarriage, congenital anomalies, and other health issues. But how far should they go?

undark.title: Book Review: A Contrarian View of How Consciousness Evolved
undark.description: In “Natural Intelligence & the Logic of Consciousness,” neuroscientist Antonio Damasio argues against the conventional theory that consciousness stems from high-level brain function and cognition, which in turn leads to feelings. Instead, he writes, our basest feelings led us to our loftiest thoughts.

undark.title: AI Presents Science with a ‘Ship of Theseus’ Problem
undark.description: Opinion | AI is being integrated into every part of the scientific process, including education, publishing, and the research itself. What does it mean if every component of the enterprise gets replaced by AI tools over time? C. Brandon Ogbunu explores what happens when science gets stripped of human involvement.

proj-syn.title: Why Following in Milei’s Footsteps Would Be Bad for Brazil
proj-syn.description: Far-right presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro holds up Argentine President Javier Milei’s economic program as a model for Brazil. But Milei's economic experiment has been a failure, leaving millions of Argentinians worse off and effectively turning their heavily indebted country into a client of the United States.

proj-syn.title: How Worried Should We Be About the Global Economy?
proj-syn.description: The risks to the global economy—including high inflation, soaring public debt, market concentration, and geopolitical volatility—are well known. But it is worth underscoring just how rare and dangerous it is for all of them to be salient at the same time.

proj-syn.title: How a Pause on Frontier AI Could Work
proj-syn.description: Whether the development of frontier AI should be paused is for policymakers to decide. But they should recognize that highly concentrated hardware supply chains make a pause feasible and, if implemented properly, likely to be sustainable.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s Latest Gift to Putin
proj-syn.description: Unable to win his foolish war against Iran, Donald Trump blames its consequences on Ukraine and uses the lie to justify ending sanctions against Russia, thereby extending that war as well. His diesel deal with the Kremlin is less about lowering gas prices for Americans and more about submitting to Vladimir Putin.

proj-syn.title: China’s Panda Diplomacy Is Losing Its Charm
proj-syn.description: Since giving a pair of giant pandas to the Smithsonian’s National Zoo in 1972 following President Richard Nixon’s visit to Beijing, China has used panda loans as a means of projecting a harmless and friendly image globally. But it was always an act—and foreign audiences are no longer falling for it.

proj-syn.title: The Blindness of China’s All-Seeing State
proj-syn.description: China's relentless surveillance has taught people to perform obedience and loyalty, while keeping their beliefs hidden. This creates a dilemma for the ruling Communist Party: repression distorts the very information the government needs to understand society.

proj-syn.title: A Stronger Renminbi Is No Quick Fix for Global Imbalances
proj-syn.description: The near-consensus among financial commentators is that China's currency is undervalued, driving global imbalances. But the renminbi's weakness reflects weak domestic demand, and pursuing currency appreciation without addressing that issue head-on would be counterproductive for everyone.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s Misguided War Against Effective Altruism
proj-syn.description: The US Department of “War” has recently begun attacking effective altruism, a movement that aims to save lives, reduce suffering, and prevent future catastrophes. Why would the Trump administration, which with great fanfare created a Department of Government Efficiency, now oppose being effective?

proj-syn.title: Futureless Russia
proj-syn.description: During past periods of chaos and brutality in Russia, such as Stalin’s Great Terror, there was generally a sense that the country was headed somewhere—that the suffering served some end, however unjustifiable the means. But the repression Russians are enduring today has only one aim: to perpetuate the state that is executing it.

proj-syn.title: Public Investment Is Fiscally Responsible
proj-syn.description: Although fiscal responsibility is the right goal for any government, it cannot be properly measured through deficits and debt targets alone. Those who demand budget cuts in the face of higher debt levels overlook the importance of public spending that strengthens the economy's productive capacity over time.

proj-syn.title: The Rise of Reputation Ops
proj-syn.description: Even as most people have grown more accustomed to spotting fake news and questioning what they see online, new technologies and older tactics familiar from Cold War psyops have created a more vexing problem. Can our shared information ecosystem survive the rise of the “rep-op”?

proj-syn.title: Will the Bardella Scandal Sink Le Pen?
proj-syn.description: The scandal over antisemitic comments made by the far-right National Rally's Jordan Bardella could die down quickly, enabling Marine Le Pen to stick to her current plan: win the 2027 presidential election and name Bardella her prime minister. But there are two other possible scenarios, neither of which would be good for Bardella.

proj-syn.title: Can China and America Handle Being Ordinary?
proj-syn.description: For at least a generation, China's "economic miracle" allowed its people to look at Americans not as inhabitants of a richer world, but as potential peers. But now the two societies are peers in a different sense, because the Chinese are increasingly suffering the same rude awakening that Americans did when their own miracle ended.

proj-syn.title: How to Improve Global Mineral Governance
proj-syn.description: The race to secure critical minerals has intensified at the same time as the international community has recognized the need for more sustainable and responsible mining practices. Translating the resulting frameworks and guidelines into concrete action will require consolidating Global South policy and advocacy networks.

proj-syn.title: A Global Debt Crisis Is Looming
proj-syn.description: After a decade of debt accumulation, higher interest rates and growing refinancing needs have left the global economy increasingly exposed to shocks. And now ongoing conflicts are driving up energy prices, fueling renewed inflationary pressures and revealing dangerous cracks in the existing debt architecture.

proj-syn.title: Europe Must Look Beyond the US and China to Solve Its Productivity Problem
proj-syn.description: Given America and China’s lead in AI and other cutting-edge innovations, it is not surprising that much of the European economic policy debate revolves around the need to emulate and catch up with these two technological superpowers. In fact, neither the US nor China offers a relevant or attractive model for Europe.

proj-syn.title: A Global Economic Recovery Built on Shaky Foundations
proj-syn.description: The latest update of the Brookings-FT TIGER survey reveals that global growth has stabilized, with both advanced and emerging market economies showing positive momentum. But amid persistent inflation and fiscal profligacy, policymakers will still be forced to push forward with structural reforms to unleash productivity growth.

proj-syn.title: The French Far Right Embraces Austerity
proj-syn.description: In a recent speech detailing her economic program, the French far-right leader Marine Le Pen offered what can only be described as a populist vision of fiscal consolidation. Whether she can make such a paradoxical formulation work will now determine her own future, and possibly that of Europe’s nationalist right.
